Commentary.Commentary: Phew. Plenty written. Plenty said. Let us take a breather. Sri Lanka have won. Period. Sri Lanka have defeated South Africa. Double period. The Islanders have beaten the Proteas in the latter's backyard. Wow. Don't feel like putting a period here, do you? But we have to. A fantastic Test match has ended and it is great to be in the Lankan camp right now, while we offer our commiserations to the Proteas. But life moves on. So does the series. Can Sri Lanka achieve what no Asian team has done? Win a Test series in South Africa? A draw in the second Test would suffice. But expect the Proteas to come back hard. Their first loss at home since March 2018, recording 6 straight wins. Join us on Thursday, February 21, 2019 at 10 am local (0800 GMT) to see whether they avoid a series defeat. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

KUSAL PERERA HAS BEEN NAMED THE MAN OF THE MATCH FOR HIS 51 AND 153 NOT OUT. On his feelings currently, he honestly says that he is tired and does not know what to say! Praises Vishwa Fernando for hanging around with him and helping the team across the line. On his own contribution, Perera says that he just did his bit with everyone else contributing their stuff.

Victorious Sri Lankan skipper, Dimuth Karunaratne, says that it was a great game. Adds that before this match, the Lankans knew that they had a great chance as their only win in South Africa before in a Test had also come at this venue, in 2011. Says that this will be a big boost to not only the players but also the fans back home. On the feelings in the dressing room during the last-wicket stand, Karunaratne smiles and says that no one was moving and everyone was praying. Adds that the feeling in the dressing room is generally very happy and that is what he wants as a captain. Has full of praises for his young side, facing a pacy attack from South Africa and also Embuldeniya, for taking his 5-fer. On Vishwa Fernando, he says that he supported Lakmal when he did not get a wicket and then with the bat, supported Kusal Perera really well. Expects his side to fight hard again in the second Test.

South African skipper, Faf du Plessis, says that it was an incredible game of cricket. Adds that he is disappointed to finish on the losing side but says that if a fan watches 60-70 runs for the last wicket and sees the team win, there is nothing better. Praises Kusal Perera for single-handedly taking the Lankans home. Admits that the Proteas were average with the bat, making 50 below par in  the first innings and then losing their way in the second. Is still struggling to answer as to how the Saffas lost 5/8 in the second innings with the ball not doing anything till that stage but then, suddenly swinging. Stresses that it was the swing which did the batsmen in, even though the spinner (Embuldeniya) took a fifer. Wants his own team to take a leaf out of how the Lankan tail wagged. On his thought process when the last-wicket stand was going on, Faf says that there were plenty of thoughts and they tried everything, protecting the target, keeping the main batsman off strike, bowling as many balls as possible to the tailender but nothing worked today. Praises Dale Steyn and laments the loss of Vernon Philander this morning, as this pitch and the conditions suited him to perfection. But is quick to add that he does not want to give any excuses, as with 220 runs to defend and 7 wickets required, he backed his bowlers to pick those on any day. Stresses that without a doubt, the unit will come back firing for the second Test but is disappointed that this is just a 2-match series.

And now. Sri Lanka. The first line of their national anthem means thus - 'Thou Mother Lanka, Oh Mother Lanka we salute, salute, salute, salute Thee!' Today, that salute goes to Kusal Perera and the entire Lankan team. Not many visiting teams have the courage to bowl first in South Africa. But they did. Restricted the Saffas to 235, probably lost it with the bat in the first innings but then, to believe that they can win with South Africa racing ahead at 251/5 in the second innings and leading by 295 deserves respect. Lasith Embuldeniya. Does he have any relation with Lasith Malinga? Nope. Probably that word Lasith itself means magic. From nowhere, the 22-year old debutant took a 5-fer, which meant that the Lankans needed 304 to win - still a daunting task but achievable. And they achieved it. Please stay tuned for the post-match presentation...

Talking about the Saffa bowlers, they strut their stuff. Bundled out the Lankans to get a 44-run lead after a modest 235 and then, in the second innings, should have taken that 10th wicket but luck eluded them. Plenty of edges went past the fielders, landing in no man's land. Steyn took a 4-fer in the first innings while Keshav Maharaj took 3 in the second. Crucially, Vernon Philander was not feeling too well with his hamstring and did not take the field at all on Saturday, which proved to be a massive blow.

About the match in total, where did South Africa lose the game? Making just 235 in the first innings with just one half centurion in Quinton de Kock? Or losing their way from 251/5 to 259 all out in the second innings? Had they made 300 in either of the innings, it could have been a different story. The second innings saw two half centurions but overall, it was an average batting display.

Okay. Now for the game summary. Let us begin in reverse order. With Embuldeniya's 5-for setting up a target of 304, Sri Lanka began well, reaching 42/0 but then slipped to 52/3 in no time. This morning, they resumed at 83/3, lost 2 wickets quickly, but the Kusal-Dhananjaya stand kept the Lankan hopes alive. However, Maharaj's late burst almost sealed the deal till the unbeaten last-wicket stand came along.
Do not forget the contribution of Vishwa Fernando. His 6 not out from 27 balls played a huge role in assisting Kusal Perera and Sri Lanka. Wow. Don't they always say, cricket is a team game?

Nothing is impossible, goes the cliche. But here, we have witnessed that nothing is indeed impossible. 206/6 - Dhananjaya de Silva falls. 98 needed with 4 wickets in hand. Match getting out of bounds for Sri Lanka. Then 206/7, 215/8 and 226/9 - 78 needed with 1 wicket in hand. Everyone dreams of a quick finish. But from there, Kusal Janith Perera has just stung the South Africans like a bee, staging an unbeaten 78-run stand with last man Vishwa Fernando and himself scoring 67 out of those!

Sri Lanka touring South Africa? Yes. Match over in 4 days. Yes. South Africa go 1-0 up. A big NO. Oh the world, wherever you are, whatever you are doing, please spare some time and visit this match centre. Kusal Perera has done a Michael Hussey. A VVS Laxman. A Paul Collingwood. A Monty Panesar. A Jimmy Anderson. Take any name you wish. In short, Kusal Perera has done nothing short of a miracle.

FOUR! SRI LANKA WIN! Unbelievable. Simply unbelievable. A length ball, outside off, Perera just angles this towards third man but it is more of an outside edge. Luckily for him, the ball flies wide of the slip fielder and races to the third man fence! Just the second 1-wicket win for the Lankans in Tests, both against South Africa!

Down the leg side, Kusal misses his tuck but the ball goes off his pads past the keeper towards fine leg. It seems like the ball is running away to the fence but fine leg gets across in time. Two runs taken, leg byes signalled and the Lankans are a boundary away from a win!
On a good length around middle and leg, Perera dabs it towards gully.
Outside off, very full, KP digs it out towards point and takes the single to retain the strike! 6 more needed to win now...
Outside off, Kusal punches this through the covers but does not run.

SIX! SLAP! That is gutsy shot and the runs required come into single digits! A length ball, around off, Kusal swings with all his might and clears mid-wicket with ease! Two men are waiting in the deep for this stroke, awaiting the top edge but it does not come. 7 more needed to win...
JUST WIDE! Around middle, Vishwa plays this uppishly, just wide of short leg and gets a single.
Short and outside off again, Fernando gets away from it.
Short ball outside off, Fernando sways away from it.
Another bouncer, around leg, Perera ducks again.
Last ball of the over. Faf du Plessis is frenetically making the field changes. Guess this is just a wastage of time, making Kusal wait...
A bouncer but way down the leg side, left alone.

TOP EDGE, SIX! Kusal Perera is riding his luck here. A short ball, around leg stump, Perera looks to pull but is in no position to do so. He gets a top edge which sails high in the air. Fine leg starts to move to his left but the ball has cleared the ropes! 14 more to win now...
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, Kusal looks to cut but gets a bottom edge towards point.

SAFE! Reduce two more from the target. 20 more needed to win. Full and around leg stump, Perera works it through mid-wicket with soft hands and immediately calls for two. The substitute Zubayr Hamza, who is on for the injured Philander is a touch slow to get to the ball. He returns a weak throw to Rabada who takes the bails off but by that time, Fernando dives in. Aleem Dar shakes his head on the run out appeal but still takes it upstairs for confirmation. Replays confirm the same in one go.
Run out? Run out? Is Fernando short? Aleem Dar wants to check...
Jaffa! But Steyn somehow fails to get the outside edge of Fernando. Bowls this on a good length around off. Vishwa hangs his bat but the ball moves away from him.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
SIX! HUGE! OH MY WORD! Perera is taking the onus on himself. That's the 50-run stand and Kusal has made most of it. Fuller ball on the pads, Perera flicks it over square leg for a big hit.
Around off, driven to the cover region.

DRAMA! Lots of it. Length ball around off, Fernando looks to defend but the ball swings away and take the outside edge. Luckily for the batsman, it falls just short of second slip. Sri Lanka want the run so Perera leaves his crease. Faf from the cordon has a shy at the non-striker's end but fails to hit the target. Had he hit, Fernando was a goner. To make matters worse, the ball runs away for four overthrows!
Length ball around off, Fernando looks to block it but it swings away from his bat.
No run taken. Good for South Africa. Rabada goes short on purpose. Perera fails to put bat to it. Steyn will now have six balls to have a go at the no. 11.
FOUR! Short ball on the leg side. Perera pulls it well and the ball crosses the ropes past the square leg boundary. Nicely played.
Wide. Unusual bounce. Too high to worry the batsman! Wide signalled by the umpire.
Good running. This one was on a good length outside off. Perera cuts it to deep point. Bavuma does well to cut just before the ropes. The batsmen take two.
Back of a length ball on the hips, tucked away to the on side.
On middle and leg, played with a straight bat.
Fuller ball on off, driven towards covers.
Kagiso Rabada is back to bowl with the second new ball.
Lovely! Length ball on off, swings away after pitching. Fernando hangs his bat and the ball goes past his outside edge.
New ball taken! Steyn will have just one delivery to have a go with it.
Steyn goes short on middle, Perera pulls it sweetly to deep square leg for a run.
Yorker again on off, Perera keeps it out.
Too wide. Tries a slower ball outside off, too far to make Kusal play at it.
Fuller on off, pushed to the off side.
BEAUTY! Yorker on middle, Perera does well to get bat to it.
Covers his stumps and keeps another one out.
Fernando blocks it. On middle, well played by Vishwa.
Fuller ball on middle and leg, Kusal on-drives it towards mid on and gets to the other end.
Outside off, Perera fails to put bat to it.
Down leg, Perera looks to reverse sweep but the ball hits his pads and rolls towards fine leg. They come back for the couple.
In the air... but falls well safe. Around off, slog swept away to cow corner. Decides against the run.
What a beauty from Steyn. Outswinger around off. Fernando some how manages to get bat to it. The ball takes the outside edge and goes to the gully region.
Takes the run now. Good from Perera. Turns his bat to the vacant mid-wicket region and gives his partner the strike.
Yorker wide outside off, Perera tries getting bat to it but fails.
How did that miss? Length ball on middle, Kusal swings but the ball misses his bat as well as the stumps.
Shot but for nothing. Outside off, cut away to deep point but refuses the run.
Full and outside off, Kusal leaves it alone.
Dale Steyn is brought back into the attack.
Outside off, Fernando plays it to point.
On the pads, flicked away to cow corner for another run.
Down the leg side, paddled away to fine leg for another couple of runs.
Around off, driven passed the cover region for a couple of runs. Required runs below 50 now.
Full in line of the stumps again. Perera looks to reverse sweep it but fails to get bat to ball.
Fuller ball on middle, blocked by Perera.
Yes he can. Not in the most convincing way. Shorter in length around off, Fernando leaves his bat hanging. The ball goes away from him and to the keeper.
Good length delivery outside off, Kusal cuts it through point and takes a single. Can Fernando survive the last ball?
Good length delivery around off, Perera pushes it to the fielder at point.
Back of a length by Olivier, Kusal pulls it to mid-wicket.

SIX! Brilliant shot. Shorter in length around middle and off, Perera rocks onto his back foot and heaves it over the fine leg fence for a maximum. The total crosses 250 with that and Sri Lanka now require 52.
Good length delivery outside off, Perera cuts it through point and straight away calls for two. The ball is wide of third man. He runs the first one hard and comes back for the second easily.
Fernando gets behind the ball and keeps this out.
Comes back in again. Perera gives room and cuts it towards backward point for a single.
Outside off, spins back in. Perera tries to cut it but the ball goes under his bat.
Covers his stumps and bunts this one down.
Kusal tried to sweep that one but missed it and was hit on the pads down leg.
Fraction short down leg, Perera pulls it towards deep square leg. He comes back easily for the second.
This time bowls it over the wicket. Olivier bowls it full this time and he gets some reverse swing on it. Vishwa does well to keep it out.
Comes 'round the wicket and bowls a shorter length delivery around off, Vishwa looks to play it and leaves his bat hanging but it goes past it to the keeper.
Length delivery outside off, Kusal cuts it towards deep point and this time takes a single.
Length delivery around off, Kusal pushes it to the fielder at point.
Length delivery around off, Kusal looks to drive but again gets an outside edge and the ball once again goes to the fielder at third man.
Edge but safe. Fuller in length outside off, Perera looks to hit it to the off side but gets an outside edge. The ball goes towards the third man region but Kusal does not take the single.
Fernando survives. On middle, blocked well by Vishwa.
Jaffa! On middle and leg, spins away from the hanging bat of Fernando.

THERE IT IS! 100 for Kusal Perera! He has got it. What a fine innings this has been. Sri Lanka have fought back well and it has been centered around him. Only if he had more partners, might have taken the Lankans home too! As for this ball, Kusal just works this around the corner on the leg side for a single to get to his 2nd Test century. Well played!
FOUR! What a shot! Goes for the reverse sweep and gets it off the middle. Gets in position early and reverse sweeps it over backward point. The ball bounces just before the ropes. Moves to 99 now.
It is getting overcast again. A big group of rain clouds is arriving. Sri Lanka could do with that. Only they can hope is that the rain just delays its arrival till Perera's century...
Fuller ball on middle and leg, swept away to square leg.
Off spinner on middle, blocked in front of him.
Good length delivery outside off, Fernando covers his off stump with a straight bat.
Bouncer.  Vishwa ducks underneath it.
Shorter in length, Kusal pulls it away to deep mid-wicket for a single.

Back of a length delivery outside leg, Perera looks to pull but takes his eyes and one hand off the bat. He cannot keep his balance either and falls down. Meanwhile behind the stumps, de Kock drops the ball.
Fuller ball outside off, Perera swings again but fails to connect.
Length ball on middle and leg. Perera looks swing hard but gets hit on the thigh pad.
Ahhh.... flighted outside off, Fernando initially goes for the big one but in the end, blocks it out.
Full and around off, watchfully kept out again.
Tossed up outside off, Vishwa looks to defend it but misses.
Flighted on the stumps, Fernando does well to block it.
Flighted on middle and off, Kusal sweeps it away to deep square leg for a single. Not the wisest decision to take a single here.
SIX! Kusal has decided to attack now. Flighted delivery outside off, Perera comes down the track and heaves it over the mid-wicket fence for a maximum. Perera now moves into his 90s.
Bluffs him by bowling it full outside off. Fernando leaves it alone.
Down the leg side, on the shorter side. No much trouble for Fernando.
Goes fuller for a change outside off, Perera drives it through covers and takes the run.
Goes short again down the leg side. Perera leaves it alone. The umpire gives it as a second bouncer of the over.
The physios are out in the middle to check on Kusal Perera. He looks fine to continue.
Short ball on leg, Perera goes for the hook but cannot connect it well. It brushes his glove, hits the helmet and lobs towards square leg.
Fuller length ball on off, Perera drives it to covers.
Tossed up on middle, Fernando blocks it to see off the over.
Flighted on off, Vishwa does well to defend it.
Vishwa Fernando walks out at number 11.

OUT! LBW! Rajitha has to walk off along with the review. Arm ball on middle and leg. Keeps going straight. Rajitha looks to flick it but misses. The ball hits him on the pads and the players appeal. Kasun takes the review but it does him no good. The ball was crashing into leg stump. Maharaj has another one and the hosts need just one more wicket for victory.
Review taken! Rajitha has been caught in front of the stumps but takes a review. Look's out.
Beautiful. flighted around off the ball spins away after pitching. Kasun looks to defend but gets beaten.
Flighted on middle and leg, Perera sweeps it and gets to the other end.
FOUR! Quicker on leg, Perera looks to sweep it. It flicks off his glove and goes to the fine leg fence for a boundary.
DRINKS! South Africa just the two wickets away from victory. Sri Lanka need more 83 runs but that looks farfetched. The important question will be, will Kusal Perera get to his 100?
Bouncer. Perera pulls it calmly towards square leg and gets a single.

Comes 'round the wicket and bowls it on middle and leg. Rajitha tucks it towards mid-wicket. Perera looks for a quick single and gets on his bike. Maharaj gets to the ball and throws it at the keeper's end. Kusal puts in a dive to get in and Keshav misses his throw. It would have been close had he hit the stumps. Very puzzling why Perera took the single off the 5th ball here.
Good length delivery on the body, Rajitha defends it.
Back of a length delivery around off, Rajitha does well to get on top of the bounce and keep it down.
Back of a length on middle and leg, Kusal pulls it to the fine leg region for a single. Perera is showing confidence in Kasun.
Slower delivery full outside off stump, Perera hits it to the fielder at cover.
Change of gloves for Kusal Perera now. All hopes are on him if Sri Lanka want to win this Test match.
Fuller ball on leg, flicked away towards mid-wicket. Kasun survives.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Angles this into the pads. Rajitha misses his flick and gets hit on his legs. The ball lobs into the hands of silly point.
Jaffa! Serves this on middle. The ball spins sharply away from Rajitha and almost gets his outside edge.
Full on off, Perera sweeps it through square leg and takes the run.
Outside off, Perera gives room and looks to cut it. He gets a bottom edge to it which goes through the legs of de Kock. They come back for the second.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Rajitha blocks it away.
Kasun Rajitha is in at no. 10.

OUT! Shorter length delivery does the trick. Duanne bowls it short, the ball rises onto the batsman. Embuldeniya looks to defend it but then sees the ball rising onto him so he takes his eyes off. The ball hits his glove and lobs to the fielder at short leg. Aiden Markram there takes a very simple catch and South Africa now just 2 wickets away from wrapping up this game. The debutant cannot repeat his heroics from the 1st innings and he has to walk back.
Good length delivery on off and middle, Lasith blocks it.
Length delivery on the thigh pad, Lasith looks to flick but it flicks off his thigh pad.
Shorter in length, Kusal pulls it away towards deep square leg and takes a single.
Sprays it down the leg side, Perera looks to flick it but misses.
Duanne Olivier back into the attack.
Played to the point region by Perera. One run added to the total.
Too close to cut, Perera still goes for it and gets a bottom edge to it.
On off, Perera reverse sweeps this through short third man for a brace.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Tucks this uppishly through square leg for one.
Loopy ball on middle and leg, Embuldeniya looks to sweep it but it hits his body.
Sprays this down the leg side, Kusal jumps a bit and looks to flick it but misses.
Well, Kusal is up on his feet. Pops in a few tablets a couple of pain-killers and is ready to fight again. Good to see. Irrespective of the result, this has been a good fightback from Sri Lanka.
The physio has come out to the middle. Kusal is looking at his index finger. Seems to have got hit on the wrist.

OUCH! Kusal Perera is down in pain. He has thrown his bat in agony and is furiously catching his left wrist. A sharp short ball, around leg stump, Perera looks to fend it away but the ball kicks off the surface and hits him hard on the glove.
Back of a length delivery on middle and leg. Embuldeniya looks to duck but gets hit on the glove. The ball goes towards the on side and they rotate the strike.
Full length delivery on the pads, Lasith flicks it away towards mid-wicket and gets a brace.
Full delivery on middle and leg, Embuldinya tucks it to the on side. The fielder at short leg hold the ball on his right and has a shy at the striker's end but he misses.
Good length delivery outside off, Perera cuts it away towards point and takes a single.
Another one coming in. Embuldeniya defends it in front of him
This one comes back into Embuldeniya who does well to get his bat to it.
Around off, pushed to the cover region.
Almost gets three in three. Arm ball outside off, Embuldeniya thinks of playing at it but withdraws at the last movement.
Lasith Embuldeniya to face the hat-trick ball.

OUT! Two in two for Maharaj. Tossed up on off, Lakmal looks to defend it but is late in his defense. The ball hits the outside edge and goes towards the slip fielder. Faf du Plessis takes a good catch there on his right. Keshav is now on a hat-trick. The tide of this match has once again shifted in favour of South Africa.
Suranga Lakmal walks out to the middle.

OUT! GONE! Three reds! What a review from Maharaj. Perfect. Arm ball on middle and leg, Dhananjaya gets low to sweep but misses the ball. He gets hit on the pads and  Keshav puts in a huge appeal. The umpire stays unmoved. The spinner requests his skipper to take it up. Faf goes up. Replays roll in and show us that there was no bat involved and the ball would have gone to hit the leg stump. De Silva played well but the 96-run stand comes to an end. Is this the opening for South Africa?
Review time! Maharaj thinks he has got Dhanajaya lbw. Is this the turning point of the match?
Shorter in length, de Silva pulls it away towards fine leg for a single.
Length delivery on off, de Silva pushes it to the fielder at point.

Length delivery around off, Kusal pushes it to covers and straight away calls for a single. Keshav Maharaj there, gets to the ball quickly and has shy at the stumps at the striker's end. He has one stump to aim at and he hits. But de Silva is inside. The ball deflects to mid-wicket and Kusal wants the second but Dhananjaya has backed up too far and sends Perera back.
Once again bowls it, Dhananjaya pulls it towards deep square leg for a single.
Once again back of a length delivery by Kagiso, de Silva pulls it to the fielder at mid-wicket.
FOUR! A very controlled pull from de Silva. Shorter in length by Rabada, Dhananjaya gets on his back foot and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Sri Lanka have crossed the 200-run mark.
Quicker one on off, Perera blocks it with a straight bat.
Down the leg side, turned away to square leg. They cross.
Gets behind this ball and defense another out.
On off this time, kept out by DDS.
Loopy ball on middle, blocked out by Dhananjaya.
Off spinner on middle, cut away through cover-point to get to the other end.
Keshav Maharaj is brought into the attack.
FOUR! Beautiful shot. Rabada offers width by bowling it outside off on a length. de Silva cuts it brilliantly through point for a boundary.
Uppish but safe. Length delivery outside off, Perera cuts it uppishly towards point. It is wide of the fielder and they take a single.
Good length delivery on middle and off, the ball comes in after pitching. Kusal looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Back of a length delivery, Kusal defends it off his back foot.
FOUR! Short, wide and punished by Perera. Length delivery outside off, Kusal cuts it through point and the ball races away to the fence.
Good length delivery outside off, Perera pushes it to the fielder at cover.
Around off, defended by de Silva.
Fuller ball outside off, Kusal drives it to mid off. Rabada there does well to stop it but cannot prevent the single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

Back of a length ball down the leg side. Perera looks to tuck it away but it goes off his glove. The ball rolls towards fine leg where they take another couple. The umpire however, gives it as leg byes.
Length on middle, Perera pushes it to the off side.
Short ball on off, pulled away through square leg for a brace.

In the air but safe. Shorter length delivery by Rabada. Perera looks to pull but is in no control of it and the ball goes uppishly towards square leg. The ball falls short of Temba Bavuma. The batsman take a single.
Full length delivery on miffle and leg, Dhananjaya hits it wide of the mid on fielder and takes a single.
FOUR! Effortless from Dhananjaya. Good length delivery around off, de Silva gets on his front foot foot and drives it through mid off for a boundary.
Length delivery on middle and leg, d Silva hits it to the fielder at mid on.
Fuller on length around off, Perera hits it straight and rotates the strike.

Good length delivery around off, de Silva looks to defend it with soft hands but gets an outside edge. The ball goes to the right of the diving slip fielder. They take a single as the fielder cannot hold onto the ball.
This one is slightly fuller around off, Perera swings and gets it past the cover region. Bavuma cleans it up near the ropes. Just two runs taken by the Sri Lankan batsmen.
Right on the money. Good length at 138kph. Perera stonewalls it.
Length again on middle and leg, Perera blocks it in front of him.
Lovely from Steyn. Gets it to move away on off. Perera gets an outside edge towards the gully region.
The short of length delivery has been cut away through square on the off side. Dot ball.
Good length ball just around off, Perera gets a bottom edge to it tries to block it.

FOUR! Dhanajaya is flirting with danger here. Length delivery outside off stump, de Silva looks to hit it on the off side but gets an outside edge on it. The ball flies past the diving Faf du Plessis at second slip and races away to the third man fence. Rabada is down on the ground in disbelief, and rightly so. 7 times out of 10 that edge goes straight to the slip fielder.
Length delivery on the stumps, de Silva defends it off his front foot.
Good shot but only a single. Shorter in length, Perera pulls it beautifully but there is a fielder at fine leg so he only gets a single.
Length delivery outside off, Perara knows where his off stump is and leaves it alone.
Good length delivery around off, Kusal pushes it to the fielder at point.
Good start! Full and going away from the southpaw. Perera looks to drive it but misses. The ball goes past his outside edge by just a few inches.

Kagiso Rabada to continue from the other end. An FYI... the second session is extended, to cover up for the overs lost due to bad light yesterday. This will be a 135-minute session, with Tea scheduled at 2.55 pm local (1255 GMT). If there is a final session, that will be from 3.15 pm-5.30 pm local (1530 GMT) and if the match still continues with overs remaining, the extra half hour will be added too! So potentially, play could go on till 1600 GMT.
First runs of this session. Full length delivery outside off, de Silva drives it through covers and gets a brace.
This time it is full on off, de Silva hits it straight to the fielder at mid off.
Back of a length delivery on off, Dhananjaya gets on his back foot and keeps it out.
Good length delivery on the stumps, Dhananjya defends it with a straight bat.
Full and again an outswinger from Steyn. De Silva handsomely drives it to the fielder at mid off.
Hint of outswing for Steyn. Bowls it full around off, Dhananjaya defends it.

We are back for the afternoon session. The umpires are out in the middle. Kusal Perera and Dhananjaya de Silva will resume their innings. It is overcast now, let's hope there is no rain later and we have a full session of play. Dale Steyn to bowl the first over of this session.
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

Philander's absence is not helping his side's cause. Steyn bowled with fire and his two-wicket over made the Proteas the favorites even more. Nothing much to speak about their bowling. The game is still on their side as they know the hosts are just a wicket away to get into the lower order. However, if Perera and Dhananjaya get the target to double digits, South Africa may start to get worried. Join us for the afternoon session in some time.

Sri Lanka won't be too disappointed with how the session panned out. For starters they began well with Fernando and Perera. The former perished and few balls later keeper-batsman, Dickwella followed suit. Kusal Perera who is known for his attacking cricket has paced his innings well. He got to his second 50 of the match and has reduced the deficit to 138.
Goes with the bouncer again, Perera gets low again. LUNCH, DAY 4.
Length ball around off, Perera taps it to the off side.
Bangs it in short, Perera ducks under it.
Over the stumps, played back to Rabada.
This one is closer to the stumps. Perera blocks it well.
Fuller length ball on the fifth stump line. Dhananjaya pushes it through covers to get to the other end.
Down leg, helped away to the fine leg region for a single.
Turn and bounce! Beautiful. Off spinner on middle, it turns away from de Silva who gets beaten.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Loopy ball on off, bunted down by Dhananjaya.
De Silva has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up ball on off, Perera steps out and pushes it to mid off. They spot the weak arm of Amla and complete the run.
Dhananjaya stays inside and keeps this one out.
Back of a length outside off, taped to the off side.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Around off again, de Silva punches it to the off side.
Length ball around off, blocked by a straight bat by de Silva.
Driven through mid off by Kusal. They pick up a single.
Kagiso Rabada back into the attack.
Fraction short, de Silva stays inside and pushes it to the off side.
Flighted ball outside off, Dhananjaya charges down the wicket and decides to pad it out.
Gets behind this ball and blocks it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! Loopy ball on middle and leg, Dhananjaya sweeps and sweeps well. It goes through square leg and away to the fence.
Outside off, Perera gets an outside edge to point.
Short on off, pulled away through mid-wicket. Elgar dives but fails to stop it. He catches his shoulder. Let's hope it is not serious. They manage to come back for the second.
Short outside off, pulled away to the man stationed at short square leg.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Short but down leg, pulled away fine towards fine leg for a single.
Down the leg side, Perera looks to pull it but fails
Short ball on off, Perera looks to block it but it comes off his glove.

Another halt in play. It is a steaming day. The temperature reads just 28 degrees Celsius but because it rained yesterday, heat seems to be dissipating from the surface. Kusal takes a whole bottle of water and nearly empties it on his head. Just 20 more minutes to Lunch, which will be a welcome break to all the players.
Nicely done. Flighted ball on off, Dhananjaya flicks it over mid-wicket. Amla from the circle stops it before the ropes and the batsmen take two.
On off, bunted down by de Silva.
Similar line and length, front foot defense shown by DDS.
Gives this air on middle and leg, Dhananjaya is solid in hi defense.
Shorter around off, Perera cuts it towards point and takes a single. Perera was looking for the second but de Silva is not interested.
Tossed up on off, Kusal looks to defend it but gets it off his inner half.
Short outside off, pulled to mid-wicket.
Looks like something has gone into de Silva's eye. He walks across to Hashim Amla and the senior helps him out a touch. The left eye it was.
Back of a length ball over the stumps, Dhananjaya hops a tad and blocks.
Slower short ball, de Silva is early into his pull and misses it.
Short on off, pulled away to the man at short mid-wicket.
On the pads, flicked away through square leg for one.
ALMOST! Short, just a prod outside off. Dhananjaya looks to guide it but it falls just short of Temba at gully. 150 up for Sri Lanka.
Flatter on middle, Perera defends it.

Good shot! Short around off by Maharaj. De Silva punches it through covers. The ball does not have the legs to go to the fence. Amla gives it a chase and saves the boundary. The batsmen pick three runs.
Flighted on the stumps by Keshav, de Silva solidly blocks it off his front foot.
Once again de Silva looks to defend the ball but fails to do so.
Slow off spinner pitching outside off, Dhananjaya looks to defend it but gets beaten.
Tossed up on middle, de Silva defends it off his front foot
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
In the air... but safe. Short ball outside off, pulled aerially towards deep square leg. No fielder there and they take a run.
FOUR! Short again, de Silva goes back into the crease and punches it through cover-point for a good looking boundary.
The batsman picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
Outside off again, guided to the man at point.
Short on off, played to the point region by the batsman.

50 for Perera! His second in this game. Looks to play the reverse sweep but gets a bottom edge to it. The ball rolls past the keeper and they come back for the second. Fine knock from Perera - playing a lone hand. Can he get to triple figures and take the Lankans closer to the total?
Perera uses his feet and hits it back to Keshav.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Down the leg side, Perera doesn't offer any shot to it. The ball goes off his pads past Quinton de Kock towards fine leg. The batsmen do not run as Perera had padded it away.
This one spins back in, Perera keeps it out.
FOUR! Too short. Didn't spin. Perera rocks back and cuts it through covers. The ball runs to the fence.
Half a shout. Down the leg side. De Silva tries tucking it but fails. De Kock collects the ball.
On the shorter side, de Silva gets bat to it and taps it to the point region.
Short again, Dhananjaya has an easy sway.
Length this time on middle and leg, turned away towards square leg for a single.
Olivier knows only one way. Goes short again, Kusal sways away from it.
Bouncer! Perera leaves it alone.
Cries of catch it but away from the short leg fielder. Looped up on leg, de Silva looks to block it but it takes the edge and flies to the on side.
Flat in line of the stumps, de Silva stonewalls it.
That ball has taken the inside edge of the batsman and thudded into his pads.

This is what balls like 43.2 can do. Straightaway de Silva steps out but is nowhere near the pitch of the ball. He looks to go over cover but miscues it. There is no one in the deep and the ball lands safely. It doesn't go the distance so they come back for the second.
Jeez! Peach! Off spinner around off, Silva comes forward to defend but the ball stays low, beats the outside edge and misses the off stump too! Great take by de Kock.
On off, reverse swept towards third man to get off strike.
Keshav Maharaj to roll his arm over.
Down the leg side, flicked away towards square leg for a single.
The short of length delivery has been cut away through square on the off side. Dot ball.
On the rib cage area, bunted down by Perera.
Back of a length, Perera blocks it.
That keeps a tad low, still a bit short. Dhanajaya pulls it towards mid-wicket for another run.
Short of a length ball on leg, de Silva pulls it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Seems like there is a problem with the ball. The umpires do not like the shape of it and they have decided to change the ball here.
DRINKS! Sri Lanka were going good but a 2-wicket over from Steyn has swung the game. Sri Lanka still need more 177 runs to win. Will this game go till the final session today?
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! Up and over! Short and outside off, Kusal slashes it over point for a boundary!
Full and around off, swinging in, Kusal looks to punch but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.

FOUR! Lucky escape! Off the inside edge but why are the South Africans appealing for LBW? Goodness me, they are thinking about the review too! Thankfully, they don't take it. Cross seam delivery on middle and leg, the ball comes in a bit after pitching. Kusal looks to punch it straight down the ground but gets an inside edge onto the pads. The ball flies past the leg stump and de Kock dives to his right but cannot stop it. Now, here is the drama. Steyn bellows out an LBW appeal and is joined by the slip cordon as well but the umpire turns it down. Dale Steyn is convinced it has hit his pad. Du Plessis in the slip cordon has a thought about taking the review and has a chat with de Kock. They eventually decide against the review. Even at normal speed, it looked like an inside edge and replays confirm there was one.
Good length delivery on off and middle, Kusal defends it off his back foot.
Once again back of a length by Olivier, de Silva pulls it away to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Shorter in length, Perera pulls it in a controlled manner and it goes all along the ground towards deep square leg. A single taken.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Perera looks to cut it but gets a bottom edge on that one.

Good length delivery on the leg side, Kusal expects it to bounce high so he jumps and looks to flick. The ball does not bounce high enough as he expected and it flicks his thigh pad and goes behind. De Kock behind the stumps dives to his right and stops the ball.
Shorter in length this time, Perera ducks underneath it.
Starts with a length delivery down the leg side, Kusal leaves it alone.
First bowling change of the day. Duanne Olivier replaces Kagiso Rabada.
Hint of away swing on this one. It is pitched outside off, de Silva shoulders arms to it.
Length delivery outside off, Dhananjaya lets it go to the keeper.
Shorter in length, this time Kusal pulls it away towards deep square leg for a single.
Good length delivery outside off, Perera jumps and looks to keep the ball down but gets and inside edge and the ball goes behind to the keeper on a bounce.
Back of a length delivery, it is Quick from Steyn. De Silva looks to defend it but gets it off the inner half and the ball goes to the on side for a single.
Full outside off, Dhananjaya drives it straight to the fielder at mid off.
Bouncer! Down leg, Perera ducks in time to let that one go over him.

Fuller ball around off, Perera drives it towards mid off and sets off for a run. The fielder there has a shy at the non-striker's end but fails to hit the target. No real backup there and they run on the overthrow.
Down the leg side on the shorter side, Perera covers his stumps and lets it go.
FOUR! Lovely! Rabada bangs it short on off, Kusal was on to it like a flash and pulled it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Comes round the wicket this time and lands it on off. Kusal taps it to the off side.
On middle and leg, played towards mid-wicket by Perera.
Full on middle and leg, Dhananjaya pushes it to the fielder at mid on.
Good length delivery on the stumps, de Silva defends it with a straight bat.
The new man is Dhananjaya de Silva.

OUT! Soft dismissal but also a great catch. This is bowled seam up by Steyn. It is full on middle, the ball stops and comes at Dickwella. Niroshan initially looks to defend but then goes for the drive. He is in between those two and ends up chipping it towards the bowler. The ball goes uppishly to the right of Dale Steyn but he shows great reflexes and takes it with one hand. Second wicket of the over and Steyn is ecstatic. Half the side back in the pavilion and now the task to chase this target looks very difficult.
Length delivery outside off, Dickwella leaves it alone.
Niroshan Dickwella is the next man in.

OUT! Steyn with the breakthrough. Cross seam delivery on off, the ball goes away from the batsman after pitching. The ball is on off, Oshada has no option but to play that one. He looks to push it but gets a thick outside edge and the ball flies to the second slip fielder. Faf du Plessis there takes a good catch at a comfortable height. And it is a huge blow for Sri Lanka as the 58-run stand is broken.
Fuller in length around off, Fernando defends it off his front foot.

Lucky escape for Rabada. Attempts to bowl a yorker but ends up serving a full toss on middle and leg. Fernando though cannot make most of it and ends up flicking it towards deep square leg for a single.
Fuller on middle and off, Fernando pushes it to the fielder at cover.
Tempting Fernando to have a go at the ball outside off, but Oshada is not interested in doing so.
Bouncer. On off stump, Oshada sways away from it.
Shorter in length outside off, Fernando leaves it alone.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Fernando cuts it straight to the point fielder.
Good shot! Length delivery outside off, Kusal cuts it beautifully but straight to the fielder at cover.
Length delivery on middle, Perera waits for it and defends it late.
Bouncer! On middle and leg, Perera ducks underneath it and lets it go to de Kock.
Length delivery around off, Kusal pushes it to the fielder at cover.
Good length delivery on middle and off, Kusal follows that boundary with a solid back foot defense.

FOUR! This time it is Perera with a good shot. Back of a length delivery outside off, Perera slashes it through covers on his back foot. The fielder at cover dives to his right but cannot get anywhere close to the ball. First boundary of the day for Perera.

FOUR! Great stroke! Full length delivery on off and middle, Fernando gets right behind that one and drives it through mid off for the first boundary of the day. Brings up the 50-run stand between these two.
Good length delivery on off this time, Oshada defends it confidently with a straight bat.
Hint of inswing on this one. Once again pitched outside off, Oshada leaves it alone.
Straighter delivery on a length, Oshada blocks it away.
Full length delivery on middle and leg, Perera flicks it away towards deep square leg for a single.
Good length delivery on middle and off, Kusal defends it with a slant bat.

That one kicked off the surface. A length ball outside off, Oshada comes forward to defend but suddenly the ball shoots up and he has to adjust. The cherry hits the bat on the higher part but drops down safely on the off side.
Full and just outside off, watchfully blocked out.
A length ball outside off, pushed towards the off side.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

Totally miscued! A normal mid off would have swallowed this. 100 UP FOR SRI LANKA. 204 more needed now. A full ball outside off, Perera looks to go over the top but mistimes his really badly. The ball goes off the toe end of the bat towards mid off and would have been a simple catch - but it isn't because there is no one there. Faf du Plessis has stationed this man who is neither at mid off, nor at long off and he cannot get to the ball in time. A single taken.
A sharp bouncer outside off, Fernando comes forward to play but then has to withdraw his bat as the ball zips through, past his nose.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.

FOUR LEG BYES! Reverse swing on offer now. The Proteas have been working on the ball for quite some time and it is slowly paying dividends. Around middle and leg, a bit too full, OF misses his flick and the ball hits him on the pads. Rabada appeals but the umpire is unmoved. The ball deflects to the fine leg fence.

Beaten! Nice comeback from Rabada. Mike Haysman on air informs that on this track, the ball speed reduces by 10-15 kph, so that much extra effort is required by the bowlers to make the ball look quick. KG bends his back, lands this on a length, forces Oshada to play at that but then gets the ball to kick and straighten, thereby beating the outside edge.
Outside off, 145 kph, Fernando is the least bit bothered. Lets de Kock feel the sting.
Down the leg side, Perera tickles it towards fine leg for a single. Leg bye signalled. 209 more to win now.

Risky shot but safe in the end. Back of a length delivery outside off, Perera looks to hit it through mid off with a slant bat. It hits high on his bat and goes uppishly wide of the cover fielder. They are able to get a run as the ball goes behind.
Back of a length delivery on off and middle, the ball swing in a bit after pitching. Oshada looks to defend but gets an inside edge. The ball goes towards fine leg and they take a single.
Slightly fuller this time, Perera pushes it wide of mid off and takes quick single.
Extra bounce on this one. Steyn bowls it on length around middle, Perera looks to defend it but gets hit on his glove.
Length delivery on off, Perera defends it with a straight bat.
Good length delivery around off, Kusal watchfully defends it and guides it to the fielder at cover.
Nice shot but for no runs. Good length delivery on off and middle, Fernando drives it straight back to the bowler.
Nice ball this. On a  length and it is straight, Oshada shows respect to this one and defends it off his front foot.
On middle and leg this time. Fernando flicks it to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Oshada defends it with straight bat.

In the air but safe. Length delivery around off, Kusal frees his arms and looks to hit it over mid off. It hits high on his bat and goes uppishly through mid off. The fielder gives it a chase and stops the ball from going to the fence. Meanwhile the batsmen come back for the third.
Length delivery on middle and leg. Perera looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
No Vernon Philander on the field yet. Seems like a hamstring niggle. Zubayr Hamza is the substitute for him.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Oshada taps it back to the bowler.
Length delivery around off, Fernando pushes it away to the fielder at point.
On the thigh pad region, Kusal flicks it away towards fine leg and rotates the strike.

Good shot! Fuller in length outside off, Oshada gets on his front foot and drives it through point. It does not have the legs to go to the fence but the batsmen get 3 runs as the fielder gives it a chase.
Sprays this down the leg side, Fernando looks to flick but misses.
Steyn starts with a length delivery on off, Perera looks to defend it, he does so from the outer half of the bat. The ball goes towards point and they take a single. First run of the day.
Dale Steyn to partner Kagiso Rabada from the other end.
Maiden to start the day. Good length delivery on middle and off, Oshada defends it to see off the over.
Back of a length delivery around off, Fernando defends it with a straight bat.
Once again on a length by Rabada. Fernando blocks it away.
Good length delivery on off and middle, Oshada tucks it to the on side with the inner half of his bat.
Length delivery outside off, Fernando calmly leaves it alone.
Rabada starts the day with bowling a good length delivery on off. Fernando gets on his back foot and defends it with soft hands. He looks for a quick single but is sent back by his partner.
We are all set to begin. Overnight batsmen Kusal Perera and Oshada Fernando walk out to the middle to resume their innings. Kagiso Rabada to bowl the first over of the day.

Hello and welcome to Day 4 of the first Test between South Africa and Sri Lanka. The visitors were given a target of 304 and started well. But lapse in concentration towards the end of Day 3 saw them lose three wickets. They were 42/0 but suddenly slipped to 52/3. They still require 221 runs but will need their batsmen to do really well if they want to get close to that total. The pendulum is swinging towards the Proteas but a wicket-less session in the morning could get it right back in the center. Two whole days left and the possibility of a draw seems very unlikely unless there are weather interruptions.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Now then, will Day 4 be the last day of the Test Match? Sri Lanka need another 221 runs and South Africa need 7 wickets, and one would believe if there is no rain which is in the forecast, it should be the final day. Do join us for all the action on Saturday. Till then, goodbye and take care!

The Lankan openers started off well, just like they did in the first innings but a wicket soon after the Tea break, led to 2 more quickly. From 42 for 0 they ended up being 52 for 3. However, Fernando and Kusal Perera are amidst a 31-run stand and if the Lankans stand any chance, the two will have to build a big partnership from here on whereas, South Africa would like to continue their good work.

The South African skipper was adamant to give Sri Lanka a big target but the debutant Embuldeniya picked a fifer and kept Sri Lanka in the game. However Faf's 90 did ensure the visitors have a stiff target of 304.

The inevitable has happened. The lights haven't improved and the umpires have called STUMPS FOR DAY 3! Another excellent day of cricket for the hosts. They are in the driver's seat at the moment. They began the day in a healthy position and then strengthened their position in the game courtesy Faf du Plessis' partnerships with de Kock and Philander.

The umpires feel the light is not good enough to continue for now and they have asked the players to walk off. PLAY STOPPED DUE TO BAD LIGHT! The covers are also seen coming on. It is not raining for now but precautionary measures are taken.
FOUR! Lovely! This one was outside off, Perera makes room and punches this through cover-point for a glorious boundary.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Loopy ball on off, Perera steps out and smacks it back but Maharaj does well to put his hand to it. That would have been a boundary if it had gone through.
Off spin on middle and leg, blocked in front of the batsman.
Flights this on off, bunted down by KP.
Off spinner on middle, stonewalled by Perera.
On the stumps again, Fernando blocks it out.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Brings the reverse sweep out and hits it through backward point. The batter takes two.
Flatter and on off, Fernando goes back and keeps it out.
Short again, this is punched through covers for another run.
Slower through the air on middle, it is worked through mid-wicket for a run.
Just outside off, Fernando plays it very late to third man and changes ends.
Aiden Markram is on now. Spin from both sides now. Maybe due to the fading lights the umpires have asked Faf to get on spinners from both ends.
On the pads, flicked away through square leg this time for one.
A fraction short, Kusal pulls it to square leg.
Around off, pushed to the cover region.
OUCH! Loopy ball on middle and leg, Perera gets low and swings at it. Markram at short leg takes one for the team. He though had his protection and doesn't look in any pain.
Around off, Perera plays it back to the bowler.
Drinks!
Shortish and on the body, it is tucked to mid-wicket.
Down the leg side, the batsman looks to flick but misses. Once again the South Africans get excited but for no reason.
Not sure this is a good shot! Short and outside off, Fernando looks to guide it through the slip cordon but misses.

Down the leg side, Fernando lets it be. Some excitement from the South African players as there was a noise as the ball passed the body. Nothing from the umpire though. Replays show that it flicked the shirt.
On the body, Perera is hit on the body, it rolls towards square leg. The batsmen take a leg bye.
Good delivery! Angles this one across the left-hander. Perera plays inside the line and gets beaten.
The arm ball to end, Fernando plays outside the line and it goes off the inner half towards square leg.
Another flighted ball, the batsman keeps it out with ease.
Floats it up on middle, Fernando luges and keeps it out.
FOUR! Easy-peasy! Down the leg side, Fernando sweeps it fine and ti races to the fine leg fence.

Flighted delivery on off, Perera pushes it to covers and sets off for a run. Steyn picks the ball up and has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses. That would have been close as Perera dropped his just outside the crease. Replays later on show that he would have been short.
Plays the sweep but it goes off the inner half towards square leg.
Keshav Maharaj is on now.
Another short one, another pull shot but once again finds the fielder. This time though the one at square leg.
Back of a length on off, kept out.
Goes for the pull but mistimes it to mid-wicket.
Back of a length on off, it is pushed to covers.

Just short! Since it was glove it did not carry! Not sure about the shot though. It is just outside off, Fernando looks to guide it down to third man, the ball goes off the glove and lands just ahead of the keeper.
Short and on the body, the batsman ducks under it.
FOUR! Up and over! Slightly fuller and Rabada pays the price. Perera stands and lofts it over mid off. A boundary results.
Stands tall and guides it to point.
Good length again on off, Perera pushes it to covers.
Back of a length on off, Perera defends it off the back foot.
Shortish and on middle, blocked out towards mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
A quick bouncer, Perera looks to pull but is beaten for pace.
A bumper and it is down the leg side, Fernando pulls it to fine leg for a single.
Short again, the batter transfers his weight on the back foot and keeps it out.
In the air... but safe! Perera too takes on the challenge of pulling it. Ends up getting a top edge towards fine leg. Lands safe, a single taken.
On the pads, nudged to fine leg for a single.
Shortish on off, Fernando looks to pull but ends up getting it off the underedge to mid-wicket.
Good running! Fernando pushes it towards point, they hesitate before going for the run, eventually go for it and complete it as the fielder misses his shy.
Back of a length again, Fernando gets behind the line and defends it onto the ground.
Back of a length on off, blocked.
The line is much starighter now, Fernando looks to flick but misses to get hit hgih on the pads.

FOUR! Streaky! Through the vacant gully region. On a length and around off, Fernando goes at it with hard hands, it hits the edge and runs down to the third man fence. Living dangerously is the batter.
On the fuller side, this is timed through the gap at the cover region for a couple.
Another short one on the body, Perera manages to keep it down towards short leg.
Kusal Perera walks in next to bat.

OUT! There goes no. 3! Olivier strikes in his first over itself! Another poor shot by another Sri Lankan batsman. It is short and just outside off. Mendis decides very late that he is going to upper cut it. The shot was never on as it there was not a lot of width on offer and also it was difficult to get on top of the bounce of that delivery. He only manages an outside edge. De Kock takes it with a leap.
Another short one, Mendis ducks under it.
On the shorter side outside off, Mendis looks to pull but is beaten by the low bounce.
Back of a length on off, Mendis is solid in defense.
Starts off with a shortish ball on the body, it is clipped towards mid-wicket.
Duanne Olivier is on now.
Now gets right behind the line and defends it onto the ground. Good over this for the visitors.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! This is more convincing! Short and outside off, Fernando stands tall and guides it through point for a boundary.

Almost drags it on! That was very loose by Fernando. It was a length ball outside off, comes back in a little. Fernando throws his bat at it but the ball goes off the inner half, over the off pole and down to the fine leg fence.
Good length on off, blocked.
Overthrows! Back of a length on off, Fernando taps it towards point and sets off for a run. The fielder there has a needless shy at the striker's end. Misses and concedes an overthrow.
Well bowled and well played! The inswinger from wide of the crease and it is very full. The batter gets his pad out of the way and strokes it to mid on.
Takes a few steps down the track to cover the swing and pushes it to mid on.
Gets this one to pitch and go straight on. Mendis blocks it by getting right behind the line.

A gem to bowl to the new batsman. On off and it moves away ever so slightly. Mendis plays the original trajectory and gets beaten. Not a lot you can do with that but just hope it does not take the edge.
Kusal Mendis walks out to the middle.

OUT! Umpire's call as it is clipping the top of middle and leg stump. Karunaratne walks back now however, he does not take the review with him. Both the set batsmen though are back in the hut and suddenly Sri Lanka are in a spot of bother. The inswinger once again gets the better of the opener. It pitches on middle and comes back in. Karunaratne looks to keep it out but fails to put bat on ball. It hits his pads and an appeal follows. The umpire thinks and then raises his finger. DK reviews as he was on his toes while playing the shot. Replays roll in and it shows that once again the on-field call is the right one. South Africa 8 wickets away and Sri Lanka need 262.
Sri Lanka review this time as Karunaratne has been give LBW. Only height can save him there.
On the off pole, blocked.
On the fuller side on off, Karunaratne strokes it nicely but can't get it past mid off.
A solid back foot defense by the batsman on his first ball.
Oshada Fernando is the next man in.

OUT! Edged and taken this time! The change of angle does the trick but to be honest a poor shot by Thirimanne. It was slightly behind the driving length, Thirimanne who got away with one earlier should have left that ball but he does not learn from his mistake. Throws his bat at it, the ball takes the outside edge and goes at a comfortable height for the second slip fielder. Faf du Plessis takes a tumbling catch. The opening stand has been broken and Sri Lanka's good start has been cut short.
On off angling away, Thirimanne covers the angle and defends it onto the ground/
Shortish and on off, Thirimanne stands tall and defends it onto the ground. He thinks of taking a run but then is sent back by his partner.
Goes for the yorker but misses it by just, Thirimanne works it to mid-wicket.
On the off pole, kept out.
A defensive stroke towards mid off to end the over. This is a good start by the Lankans.
FOUR! Top shot! There was a short mid-wicket and a mid on in place but Karunaratne has found the gap brilliantly. Full and on the pads, DK whips it through the gap and it reaches the fence.

NOT OUT! Missing the off pole and by a long way! A poor review in the end by South Africa. They have lost one now. This starts from outside off, it comes back in a little. Karunaratne looks to make a leave but the ball hits the back pad. An appeal follows but the umpire shakes his head. After a chat with his teammates, Faf signals the 'T'. Replays roll in and it shows the on-field call is the right one.
Review time! An appeal for an LBW has been turned down. South Africa review. It did come back but I don't think it has come back enough.
Well played again! Extra bounce there for Philander as he lands it on off, Karunaratne tries to defend but it hits the sticker of the bat.
On the pads, the batter looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. Philander starts appealing but then bails out.
On the fuller side, it is hit back to the bowler.
Lands it on off, Thirimanne pushes it to covers.
Bowled on the off pole again, it is guided to point.
On off, blocked.
The fullest delivery by Rabada in this spell, Karunaratne works it towards mid-wicket for a quick run.
Goes shorter this time and closer to the off pole, defended.

Play and a miss! Loose shot that. Wasn't quite full enough to drive, Karunaratne still goes for it but gets beaten. Now the, Ultra Edge just shows that there was a spike as the ball passes the bat. South Africa did appeal but it was a very soft one. Another reprieve for a Sri Lankan batsman. How much will this cost them?
On the stumps, Thirimanne goes back and keeps it out.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
On the pads, it is worked to the man at fine leg. A single taken.
The ball however, is not doing a lot here as Karunaratne gets behind the line and keeps it out with ease.
On the off stump again, Karunaratne pushes it back to the bowler. Top bowling this, keeps landing it on one area and looking to move it both ways.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On the off pole, kept out.
Slightly short but down the leg side, ducked under.
Works it with the angle through square leg for a single.
On the shorter side on off, Karunaratne does exceedingly well to take one hand off the handle and block it out.
Back of a length on off, Karunaratne stands tall and defends it.
From around the wicket angles it into the off pole, Karunaratne blocks it off the front foot.
A more comfortable leave this time as this one is wider to the off pole.
Good leave in the end! That pitches just about outside off, comes back in just a little. Thirimanne plants his front foot forward and shoulders arms. The ball goes really close past the front pad.
Back of a length on off, defended by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On the pads, the batter tries to work it on the leg side but misses. It hits his pads and rolls towards square leg. The batsmen take a leg bye.
Goes back to bowling it on off, it is blocked out.
A little too straight, this is tucked around the corner for a couple.

FOUR! Through the gap between second and third slip! How fortunate was that? Dishes out the full delivery, wanting the batsman to drive. Thirimanne goes for it but gets an outside edge. It flies between du Plessis and Elgar, both do not go for it and it races to the fence.
A bumper down the leg side, Thirimanne ducks under it with ease.
Continues bowling it on off, blocked.
Goes back to bowling length on off, Thirimanne is solid in defense.
Shortish and on the body, LH does well to nudge it to short leg.
Well bowled! 7 good deliveries by the African bowlers so far. Length around off, shapes outwards after landing. Thirimanne's outside edge is beaten.
Kagiso Rabada to bowl from the other end.
Well left! In the 5th stump channel, DK shoulders arms. Good testing over comes to an end.
Beaten for the third time in a row! Gets one to leave the batsman again from a length. Karunaratne is half-forward as he tries to block it but the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
BEATS THE OUTSIDE EDGE! This is top class bowling. The last one came back in, this one pitches on off and it shapes away. Karunaratne tries to defend but gets beaten.
Cut him into half! Back of a length ball and outside off, it jags back in sharply. Karunaratne looks to defend but is beaten by the inward movement. It goes between bat and pad and over the off pole.
Bowls it on off again, Karunaratne gets behind the line once again and blocks it out.
Starts off with a length ball around off, it comes back in a little after pitching. Karunaratne works it to the man at mid-wicket.

We are back for the final session! Around 37 overs to go so we are in for a long session. The Lankan openers will resume their innings. Karunaratne will be on strike and he will face Vernon Philander. Here we go...
... Day 3, Session 3 ...

Clearly this session belonged to Sri Lanka. They wrapped up the last 5 wickets of South Africa for just 32 runs, courtesy a 5-wicket haul from debutant Lasith Embuldeniya. With the target of 304 required, both the openers have seen off the 8 overs before Tea and the team total now reads 28/0. They require another 276 runs. The job is not done here for the openers and they will have to bat well post Tea. South Africa do not need to press the panic button yet and will look to take early wickets in the last session. The final session of the day begins in a while. Stay tuned for updates.
Fuller on middle and leg, driven towards mid on for one. THAT WILL BE TEA ON DAY 3.
On the leg side, Karunaratne taps it in front of him.
Similar line, Thirimanne works it away through square leg for one.
On middle and leg, turned towards mid-wicket.
Flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Loopy ball on the leg side, Karunaratne looks to tuck it but it goes off his thigh pad and settles in the hands of the short leg fielder.
Keshav Maharaj to roll his arm over.
Length delivery outside off, Thirimanne looks to play it but misses.
Back of a length on the stumps, Lahiru defends it off his back foot.
Back of a length on off, Karunaratne drives it through covers and gets 3 runs.
Length delivery outside off, Thirimanne drives it beautifully through point. The ball does not have the legs to go to the fence, though the batsmen are able to get 3 runs.
FOUR! That is a wonderful shot.Back of a length delivery on off, Thirimanne rocks onto his back foot and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Good length delivery outside off stump, Thirimanne looks to play it with vertical bat but gets an inside edge. The ball then goes towards the on side.
Full and straight on off, Karunaratne drives it to the fielder at mid off.
Length delivery on off, Dimuth defends it.
Full and straight outside off, Karunaratne shoulders arms to it. Interestingly the ball keeps low and reaches the wicket-keeper on a bounce.
On middle and leg, Lahiru tucks it to the on side and takes a single.
Good length delivery on off and middle, Thirimanne defends it with a straight bat.
Good leave. Length delivery outside off, Lahiru covers his off stump and leaves it alone close to his stumps.
FOUR! Full and straight on middle and off, Dimuth hits it straight through mid off for a boundary.
Length delivery on off, Dimuth keeps it out.
Fuller length delivery on off, Karunaratne defends it confidently.
Good length delivery outside off, Dimuth looks to drive it but the ball misses the outside edge.
Length delivery on off, Karunaratne pushes it to the fielder at mid off.
On middle and leg, Karunaratne flicks it away to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Good length delivery on middle and off, Lahiru defends it to see off the over.
Once again fuller length delivery outside off, Thirimanne looks to play it but misses.
Close! Length delivery outside off, Thirimanne looks to push it but misses. The ball misses the outside edge by just a whisker.
Fuller length delivery on off, Lahiru blocks it away.
Full on middle and off, Lahiru defends it with a straight bat.
Back of a length on the thigh pads, Thirimanne looks to flick it across but he misses. The ball hits him on his thigh pad.
Full on middle and leg, Thirimanne flicks it away towards the fielder at fine leg for a single.
Back of a length outside off, Karunaratne hits it towards cover and gets to the other end.
On the thigh pad region, this time Lahiru is able to flick it away to the fine leg region for a single.

In the air but safe. Good length delivery on the body of Thirimanne. Lahiru looks to tuck it on the onb side but ends up gloving it. The ball lobs uppishly towards the mid-wicket region but is short of Keshav Maharaj there.
Full on off and middle, Lahiru hits it towards mid-wicket with the inner half of his bat.
Good length delivery around off, Thirimanne blocks it with a straight bat.
Good shot! Full outside off, Thirimanne drives it through covers. He does not time it well so he only gets a single.
Good length delivery outside off, Lahiru looks to push it away but gets beaten.
Back of a length delivery on the body, Lahiru confidently defends it.

FOUR! Edgy but they will take it. Length delivery outside off, the ball goes away with the angle. Thirimanne looks to drive it through covers but gets an outside edge. The ball flies through the vacant gully region for a boundary.
Full on off this time by Philander, Thirimanne defends it with a straight bat.
Full length delivery outside off, Thirimanne leaves it alone.
Vernon Philander to share the cherry.
Kept out watchfully towards the mid-wicket region off a good length.
Bouncer! Outside off, Dimuth ducks and lets the ball go.
Short of a length on the hips, tucked away by Lahiru for a single down to fine leg.
Just outside off on a good length, Thirimanne sticks his bat out to defend. The ball catches the inside edge and runs towards square leg.
Over the wicket to Thirimanne, Steyn delivers it on a good length on middle. It is pushed back to the bowler.
Around the wicket on a length, worked away by Karunaratne for a single to deep fine leg. Sri Lanka are away.
